items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat non-object health records as malformed**

When `errors.jsonl` contains a syntactically valid non-object line such as `null` or `[]`, `json.loads(line)` returns `None` or a list and the `.get` call raises `AttributeError`, which this handler does not catch. The newly added explicit `prune` path invokes this helper, and `main` does not catch `AttributeError`, so `contextdb prune` crashes after database retention instead of retaining the malformed health-log line. Validate that the parsed value is a mapping (or catch `AttributeError`) before reading `ts_utc`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:b9acaa39

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate configured health retention before pruning**

A config containing `"operations": null` passes `load_config`, because the validation routine never validates the `operations` section, but this newly added direct subscription then raises an uncaught `TypeError`. Likewise, an invalid retention value is only discovered after the event-retention transaction has already run. Validate `operations.error_log_retention_days` as a non-negative integer during config loading so `prune` either runs fully or rejects the configuration before mutating the database.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:b9acaa39

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse symlinked health logs before rewriting**

When a project contains a symlink at `.claude/contextdb/health/errors.jsonl`, the new explicit `prune` path follows it here and rewrites the link target with retained log entries. The new descriptor checks protect only directories, and the Codex receiver's symlink scan is not used by the normal CLI, so a tracked or pre-existing health-log symlink can cause `contextdb prune` to modify a file outside the ContextDB tree. Reject symlinked health-log files or use no-follow descriptor-relative I/O before reading and writing them.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L72-L72](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/4b9cf2a3767f4279bbf372ddf405bca3aa18a68e/AGENTS.md#L72-L72)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate health artifacts before committing prune**

The new no-follow descriptor prevents an outside-file rewrite, but it is invoked only after the retention/size-cap transaction has committed and `VACUUM` may have run. When `errors.jsonl` is a symlink, FIFO, unreadable, or invalid UTF-8 file, this call raises and `contextdb prune` exits 2 after permanently deleting events (a symlinked log with an expired event leaves zero events). Open/validate the health paths before the database mutation, or otherwise make this partial-success behavior explicit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep generated recovery commands independent of uv**

For an installed project that meets the documented standard-library/Python-only runtime requirement but has no `uv` on `PATH`, every recovery verification command now fails before reaching `contextdb_cli.py`; the installer still configures the hooks with bare `python3`. Local `uv run --help` defines `--no-project` only as “Avoid discovering the project or workspace,” so it does not make the `uv` executable optional. Keep `python3` here or install and document `uv` as a runtime dependency.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:634cb327

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize health-log pruning with error appends**

When an explicit `prune` overlaps a hook calling `record_error`, that hook appends to `errors.jsonl` with `O_APPEND` while this code rewrites the file. An append that lands after the read but before this truncate is silently discarded, losing a newly recorded health error. Use a shared lock or an append-safe/atomic retention strategy for the health log.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve Windows-compatible hook imports**

On native Windows, `fcntl` is unavailable, so importing `contextdb.hook` now fails before the existing `msvcrt` locking path in `spool.py` can run. The still-shipped `settings.windows.example.json` installs `contextdb_hook.py`, and the CLI also imports `process_payload`, so Windows installations lose both lifecycle ingestion and CLI access. Provide a Windows-compatible lock/no-follow fallback or keep these POSIX-only imports out of the shared import path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L71-L71](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/3d47887757114e257f8d8019a300a884a5c39561/AGENTS.md#L71-L71)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.body: fixed:9f9b26f4 — the release contract is POSIX-only (Linux/macOS) as of 2.0.0+dotfiles.9, stated in README and CHANGELOG; `fcntl` is imported inside the two locking functions, so importing `contextdb.hook`/`contextdb.util`, the CLI and `--help` work without it, and the locking call raises a clear RuntimeError before any write instead of proceeding unlocked (import regression test added). The Windows settings example is documented as a legacy template (orchestrator disposition).

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore already-removed quarantine files during retention**

When an explicit `contextdb prune` overlaps another explicit prune or a SessionEnd retention pass, both callers can observe the same expired quarantine file before either unlinks it; the second `unlink()` then raises `FileNotFoundError`. This makes the explicit command exit 2 before database pruning, while the hook swallows the exception and skips event retention. Catch a vanished-file error (or serialize quarantine cleanup) so concurrent maintenance remains successful.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:a536af5b

items.author: moriya-fumio-thd
items.body: fixed:a536af5b — the quarantine sweep tolerates only `FileNotFoundError` per entry (a concurrent pruner or hook removed it first) and continues; any other `OSError` still propagates (regression covers the stat race, the unlink race and a PermissionError that must still fail) (orchestrator disposition).
